report.answer_text:
On April 2, 2025, which President Donald Trump called “Liberation Day,” the U.S. announced two tiers of new tariffs: (whitehouse.gov)
A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. goods imports, effective April 5, 2025. (whitehouse.gov)
Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, scheduled to start April 9, 2025. These rates replaced the 10% baseline for covered goods from those partners; they weren’t added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)
| Trading partner | Rate announced April 2 |
|---|---:|
| European Union | 20% |
| Japan | 24% |
| South Korea | 25% |
| India | 26% |
| Taiwan | 32% |
| China | 34% |
| Vietnam | 46% |
| Cambodia | 49% |
| Lesotho | 50% |
The full list is in Annex I of the executive order. China’s 34% was the newly announced tariff, not its total tariff burden. (whitehouse.gov)
Canada and Mexico stayed under separate tariff rules. The new tariffs also excluded some products, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and certain energy products, as well as steel, aluminum, autos, and auto parts already covered by separate tariffs. The rates above are what was announced on April 2; many were changed or paused shortly afterward. (whitehouse.gov)

quotes.text: Using his IEEPA authority, President Trump will impose a 10% tariff on all countries.
This will take effect April 5, 2025 at 12:01 a.m. EDT.
All other countries will continue to be subject to the original 10% tariff baseline.

quotes.text: Such rates of duty shall apply with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 9, 2025

Furthermore, except as otherwise provided in this order, at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 9, 2025, all articles from trading partners enumerated in Annex I to this order imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to the country-specific ad valorem rates of duty specified in Annex I to this order.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state that country-specific ad valorem duties for trading partners listed in Annex I take effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 9, 2025, which backs the claim that higher reciprocal tariffs for dozens of partners were scheduled to start that date (the quotes do not explicitly say 'higher' or give the count of 'dozens', but the Annex I list of partners and rates covers that).
pages.page_reason: The page states that country-specific rates for trading partners listed in Annex I were to apply starting April 9, 2025, but it does not say that the list covered dozens of partners.

claims.sentence: These rates replaced the 10% baseline for covered goods from those partners; they weren’t added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)

quotes.text: The additional ad valorem duty on all imports from all trading partners shall start at 10 percent and shortly thereafter, the additional ad valorem duty shall increase for trading partners enumerated in Annex I to this order at the rates set forth in Annex I to this order.

Sec. 3. Implementation. (a) Except as otherwise provided in this order, all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes say the duty starts at 10% for all imports and increases for Annex I partners to higher Annex I rates, but they never state that the higher rate replaced the 10% rather than being added on top of it.
pages.page_reason: The page says country-specific rates apply from April 9 but does not state that they replace the 10% baseline or are not added on top of it.
